segments.tr: ## 📚 Istilah Hari Ini

segments.src: - **Time series** — demand recorded at regular, evenly spaced intervals (weekly, monthly), the raw input to any statistical forecast.
segments.tr: - **Deret waktu** — permintaan yang dicatat pada interval teratur, berjarak sama (mingguan, bulanan), input mentah untuk peramalan statistik apa pun.

segments.src: - **Moving average** — a forecast equal to the simple average of the last N periods; all N count equally, everything older counts not at all.
segments.tr: - **Rata-rata bergerak** — peramalan yang sama dengan rata-rata sederhana dari N periode terakhir; semua N dihitung sama, semuanya yang lebih lama tidak dihitung sama sekali.

segments.src: - **Exponential smoothing** — a forecast updated as `old forecast + alpha x (actual - old forecast)`, giving recent periods geometrically more weight.
segments.tr: - **Penghalusan eksponensial** — peramalan diperbarui sebagai `peramalan lama + alpha x (aktual - peramalan lama)`, memberikan periode terbaru bobot geometris lebih banyak.

segments.src: - **Smoothing constant (alpha)** — the 0-to-1 dial controlling responsiveness; low means stable and slow, high means reactive and jumpy.
segments.tr: - **Konstanta penghalusan (alpha)** — dial 0-ke-1 yang mengontrol responsivitas; rendah berarti stabil dan lambat, tinggi berarti reaktif dan berfluktuasi.

segments.src: - **MAPE** — mean absolute percentage error; average miss expressed as a percent of actual demand, which makes it comparable across items but unreliable when demand is near zero.
segments.tr: - **MAPE** — mean absolute percentage error; miss rata-rata dinyatakan sebagai persentase dari permintaan aktual, yang membuatnya dapat dibandingkan di seluruh item tetapi tidak dapat diandalkan ketika permintaan mendekati nol.

segments.src: - **Bias (tracking signal)** — the running sum of signed errors, divided by MAD; it reveals whether misses are one-sided rather than merely large.
segments.tr: - **Bias (sinyal pelacakan)** — jumlah kesalahan yang ditandatangani secara berjalan, dibagi dengan MAD; itu mengungkapkan apakah miss adalah satu sisi daripada hanya besar.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — (b).** A longer window averages over more history, so it smooths noise but lags real changes; more data does not guarantee lower error.
segments.tr: *Jawaban: **Q1 — (b).** Jendela yang lebih panjang rata-rata lebih banyak riwayat, jadi itu meratakan noise tetapi tertinggal dari perubahan nyata; lebih banyak data tidak menjamin kesalahan lebih rendah.

segments.src: **Q2 — O.** Alpha is the fraction of the latest error fed back into the forecast, so a bigger alpha means a bigger correction.
segments.tr: **Q2 — O.** Alpha adalah fraksi kesalahan terbaru yang dikembalikan ke peramalan, jadi alpha yang lebih besar berarti koreksi yang lebih besar.

segments.src: **Q3 — (c).** MAD and MAPE discard the sign of the error, so a small MAPE can hide a persistent one-directional miss.
segments.tr: **Q3 — (c).** MAD dan MAPE membuang tanda kesalahan, jadi MAPE kecil dapat menyembunyikan miss satu arah yang persisten.

segments.src: A growing positive bias means actual demand keeps exceeding your forecast — a structural cause to investigate, not random noise.*
segments.tr: Bias positif yang berkembang berarti permintaan aktual terus melampaui peramalan Anda — penyebab struktural untuk diselidiki, bukan noise acak.*

ja.title: [ロジスティクス 101 #3] すべての予測は間違っている — プロはそれをどうやってより正確にするのか

segments.src: > Demand forecasting isn't fortune-telling; it's a set of simple arithmetic rules for turning past sales into next week's order quantity — and for measuring how badly you missed.
segments.tr: > 需要予測は占いではなく、過去の売上を来週の発注量に変換し、どの程度外したかを測定するための一連の単純な算術ルールです。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日のコンセプト

segments.src: Every business that holds inventory has to answer one question over and over: **how many should we order?** Order too many and you've buried cash in a warehouse.
segments.tr: 在庫を保有するすべてのビジネスは、何度も同じ質問に答える必要があります。**何個発注すべきか？**多すぎる量を発注すると、現金を倉庫に埋めてしまいます。

segments.src: Order too few and you're apologizing to customers.
segments.tr: 発注量が少なすぎると、顧客に謝罪することになります。

segments.src: Nobody knows the true answer.
segments.tr: 誰も本当の答えは知りません。

segments.src: So supply chain planners do the next best thing: they build a **forecast** from the demand history they already have, then track how wrong it turns out to be.
segments.tr: そのため、サプライチェーン計画者は次善の策を講じます。すでに持っている需要履歴から**予測**を構築し、それがどの程度間違っているかを追跡します。

segments.src: **Time series analysis** is the starting point.
segments.tr: **時系列分析**が出発点です。

segments.src: A time series is just demand recorded at regular intervals — units per week, cases per month.
segments.tr: 時系列は、定期的な間隔で記録された需要にすぎません — 週単位での数量、月単位でのケース数です。

segments.src: Planners assume any series is a blend of four ingredients:
segments.tr: 計画者は、すべての時系列が4つの要素の組み合わせであると仮定します。

segments.src: - **Level** — the baseline, "we sell about 100 a week"
segments.tr: - **レベル（水準）** — ベースライン、「週に約100個売れます」

segments.src: - **Trend** — a steady drift up or down
segments.tr: - **トレンド** — 着実な上昇または下降傾向

segments.src: - **Seasonality** — a repeating pattern (December spikes, summer slumps)
segments.tr: - **季節性** — 繰り返されるパターン（12月のピーク、夏の落ち込み）

segments.src: - **Noise** — random wobble that will never be predictable
segments.tr: - **ノイズ** — 予測不可能なランダムな変動

segments.src: The whole game is separating the signal (level, trend, seasonality) from the noise.
segments.tr: 全体的なゲームは、シグナル（レベル、トレンド、季節性）をノイズから分離することです。

segments.src: Forecasting methods differ mainly in *how much weight they give to recent data*.
segments.tr: 予測方法の主な違いは、*最近のデータにどの程度の重みをつけるか*にあります。

segments.src: **Moving average** is the bluntest tool.
segments.tr: **移動平均**は最も単純なツールです。

segments.src: Take the last N periods, average them, call that your forecast:
segments.tr: 最後のN期間を取り、それらの平均を求め、それを予測と呼びます。

segments.src: Forecast for next period = (sum of last N periods) / N
segments.tr: Forecast for next period = (sum of last N periods) / N

segments.src: The only real decision is N.
segments.tr: 唯一の実際の決定はNです。

segments.src: A 3-week moving average reacts fast to change but jumps around; a 12-week average is smooth and calm but slow to notice that demand has actually shifted.
segments.tr: 3週間の移動平均は変化に素早く反応しますが、変動が大きくなります。12週間の平均は滑らかで安定していますが、需要が実際にシフトしたことに気づくのが遅くなります。

segments.src: Its structural weakness: every period in the window counts equally, and everything older counts zero.
segments.tr: その構造的な弱点は、ウィンドウ内のすべての期間が等しくカウントされ、それより古いものはすべてゼロになることです。

segments.src: Last week and ten weeks ago get identical votes.
segments.tr: 先週と10週間前は同じ投票権を得ます。

segments.src: **Exponential smoothing** fixes that.
segments.tr: **指数平滑法**がそれを修正します。

segments.src: It keeps one number — the previous forecast — and nudges it by a fraction of the most recent miss:
segments.tr: 1つの数値（前回の予測）を保持し、最新の外れの一部だけ調整します。

segments.src: New forecast = Old forecast + alpha x (Actual - Old forecast)
segments.tr: New forecast = Old forecast + alpha x (Actual - Old forecast)

segments.src: `alpha` is the **smoothing constant**, a number between 0 and 1.
segments.tr: `alpha`は**平滑化定数**で、0から1の間の数値です。

segments.src: At alpha = 0.1 the forecast barely budges; at alpha = 0.5 it chases recent sales hard.
segments.tr: alpha = 0.1のとき、予測はほとんど変わりません。alpha = 0.5のときは、最近の売上を強く追跡します。

segments.src: Under the hood this gives every past period a weight that shrinks geometrically as it ages — recent data matters most, old data fades but never fully disappears.
segments.tr: 内部では、過去のすべての期間に幾何級数的に減少する重みを付与します。最近のデータが最も重要で、古いデータは薄れますが、完全には消えません。

segments.src: And it's cheap: you store two numbers per item, not twelve months of history.
segments.tr: そして、安価です。アイテムごとに2つの数値を保存するだけで、12ヶ月の履歴を保存する必要はありません。

segments.src: That's why it runs inside most ERP systems on millions of SKUs overnight.
segments.tr: そのため、ほとんどのERPシステム内で数百万のSKUに対して一夜で実行されます。

segments.src: One honest limitation: this basic version tracks level only.
segments.tr: 1つの正直な制限は、この基本的なバージョンはレベルのみを追跡することです。

segments.src: If your demand has a real trend or seasonality, plain exponential smoothing will lag behind it forever.
segments.tr: 需要に実際のトレンドまたは季節性がある場合、単純な指数平滑法はそれに永遠に遅れます。

segments.src: Extended versions (Holt's method for trend, Holt-Winters for trend plus seasonality) exist precisely for that.
segments.tr: 拡張バージョン（トレンド用のホルト法、トレンドと季節性用のホルト・ウィンターズ法）はまさにそのために存在します。

segments.src: Finally, **forecast error** — the part beginners skip and professionals live in.
segments.tr: 最後に、**予測誤差** — 初心者はスキップし、プロが生きる部分です。

segments.src: Two questions matter, and they're different:
segments.tr: 2つの質問が重要であり、それらは異なります。

segments.src: - *How far off are we?* → **MAD** (mean absolute deviation, average miss in units) or **MAPE** (mean absolute percentage error, average miss in percent)
segments.tr: - *どの程度外れていますか？* → **MAD**（平均絶対偏差、ユニット単位での平均的な外れ）または**MAPE**（平均絶対パーセント誤差、パーセンテージでの平均的な外れ）

segments.src: - *Which direction are we off?* → **bias**, the running sum of signed errors
segments.tr: - *どの方向に外れていますか？* → **バイアス**、符号付き誤差の累積合計

segments.src: MAD and MAPE ignore the sign, so a +10 and a -10 look like equally good performance.
segments.tr: MADとMAPEは符号を無視するため、+10と-10は同等のパフォーマンスに見えます。

segments.src: Bias catches the thing that actually hurts: forecasting low every single week means quietly running out of stock every single week.
segments.tr: バイアスは実際に痛い問題を見つけます。毎週低い予測をすることは、毎週静かに在庫がなくなることを意味します。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活での例

segments.src: You handle replenishment for a regional coffee chain's distribution center outside Denver.
segments.tr: デンバー郊外の地域的なコーヒーチェーンの配送センターの補充を担当しています。

segments.src: One SKU: cases of oat milk.
segments.tr: 1つのSKU：オートミルクのケース。

segments.src: The last six weeks of actual demand: **100, 108, 96, 104, 112, 108** cases.
**Moving average.** A 3-week average gives you `(104 + 112 + 108) / 3 = 108` cases for next week.
segments.tr: **移動平均。**3週間の平均は来週の`(104 + 112 + 108) / 3 = 108`ケースを与えます。

segments.src: A 6-week average gives `104.7`.
segments.tr: 6週間の平均は`104.7`を与えます。

segments.src: Same data, different answer — the shorter window has noticed the recent uptick, the longer one hasn't yet.
segments.tr: 同じデータ、異なる答え — より短いウィンドウは最近の上昇に気づいていますが、より長いものはまだ気づいていません。

segments.src: **Exponential smoothing.** Your system forecast 102 for last week, actual came in at 108, so the error was +6.
segments.tr: **指数平滑法。**あなたのシステムは先週102と予測しましたが、実際は108だったため、誤差は+6でした。

segments.src: With alpha = 0.2:
segments.tr: alpha = 0.2の場合：

segments.src: Notice it moved only 1.2 cases, not 6.
segments.tr: 6ではなく1.2ケースしか移動しなかったことに注意してください。

segments.src: That's deliberate — with alpha low, the system assumes most of that miss was noise, not a real shift.
segments.tr: それは意図的です。alphaが低い場合、システムはその誤差のほとんどがノイズであり、実際のシフトではないと仮定します。

segments.src: If oat milk demand really is climbing, a 0.2 alpha will take several weeks to catch up.
segments.tr: オートミルクの需要が本当に上昇している場合、0.2のalphaは追いつくのに数週間かかります。

segments.src: **Now the error check.** Over four recent weeks your errors (actual minus forecast) were **+4, -5, +12, +6**.
segments.tr: **エラーチェックを行います。**過去4週間のエラー（実際値から予測値を差し引いたもの）は**+4, -5, +12, +6**でした。

segments.src: - MAD = (4 + 5 + 12 + 6) / 4 = **6.75 cases** — you're typically off by about 7 cases
segments.tr: - MAD = (4 + 5 + 12 + 6) / 4 = **6.75ケース** — 通常、約7ケース外れています

segments.src: - MAPE ≈ **6.3%** — respectable for a single SKU at store level
segments.tr: - MAPE ≈ **6.3%** — 店舗レベルの単一SKUとしては実績があります

segments.src: - Bias = 4 - 5 + 12 + 6 = **+17 cases** — and *that's* the alarm
segments.tr: - バイアス = 4 - 5 + 12 + 6 = **+17ケース** — そして*これが*アラームです

segments.src: Three of four weeks you forecast too low, and the misses stack up.
segments.tr: 4週間のうち3週間は低すぎる予測を行い、誤差が積み重なります。

segments.src: A common check is the **tracking signal** (`bias divided by MAD`, here 17 / 6.75 ≈ 2.5); many planners investigate once it drifts past roughly ±4.
segments.tr: 一般的なチェックは**トラッキング信号**（`バイアスをMADで除いたもの`、ここでは17 / 6.75 ≈ 2.5）です。多くの計画者はこれが大体±4を超えたら調査を始めます。

segments.src: You're not there yet, but the direction is one-sided.
segments.tr: まだそこには達していませんが、方向は片方向です。

segments.src: Something real is happening — a new store on the route, a seasonal shift, a competitor closing — and no amount of tuning alpha will fix a cause your history doesn't contain yet.
segments.tr: 何か実際のことが起きています — ルート上の新しい店舗、季節的なシフト、競合他社の閉鎖 — そしてalphaをチューニングしても、履歴にまだ含まれていない原因は修正できません。

segments.src: That last move is what separates a demand planner from a spreadsheet.
segments.tr: その最後のステップが、需要計画者とスプレッドシートを区別するものです。

segments.src: The math tells you *that* you're wrong; you go find out *why*.
segments.tr: 数学は*あなたが間違っていること*を教えてくれます。あなたは*なぜ*なのかを見つけに行きます。

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3行要約

segments.src: 1. A demand time series is level + trend + seasonality + noise, and forecasting means extracting the first three while ignoring the last.
segments.tr: 1. 需要時系列はレベル + トレンド + 季節性 + ノイズであり、予測とは最初の3つを抽出しながら最後のものを無視することを意味します。

segments.src: 2. Moving average weights the last N periods equally; exponential smoothing weights recent data more via `New forecast = Old forecast + alpha x error`, using far less stored data.
segments.tr: 2. 移動平均は最後のN期間に等しい重みをつけます。指数平滑法は`新しい予測 = 古い予測 + alpha x 誤差`を通じて最近のデータにより高い重みをつけ、保存されるデータははるかに少なくなります。

segments.src: 3. Track both size of error (MAD, MAPE) and direction of error (bias) — consistent one-sided misses mean your method is broken, not just noisy.
segments.tr: 3. 誤差の大きさ（MAD、MAPE）と誤差の方向（バイアス）の両方を追跡します。一貫した片方向の誤差は、あなたの方法が単にノイズが多いのではなく、壊れていることを意味します。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自己チェッククイズ

segments.src: **Q1.** You switch from a 3-week moving average to a 12-week moving average.
segments.tr: **Q1。**3週間の移動平均から12週間の移動平均に切り替えます。

segments.src: What happens?
segments.tr: 何が起こりますか？

segments.src: - (a) The forecast reacts faster to sudden demand changes
segments.tr: - (a) 予測は急激な需要変化に素早く反応します

segments.src: - (b) The forecast becomes smoother but slower to react
segments.tr: - (b) 予測はより滑らかになりますが、反応が遅くなります

segments.src: - (c) Forecast error is guaranteed to drop
segments.tr: - (c) 予測誤差が必ず減少します

segments.src: - (d) Seasonality is automatically removed
segments.tr: - (d) 季節性は自動的に削除されます

segments.src: **Q2.** In exponential smoothing, a *higher* alpha (say 0.5 instead of 0.1) makes the forecast respond more strongly to the most recent period's error.
segments.tr: **Q2。**指数平滑法では、*高い* alpha（たとえば0.1の代わりに0.5）により、予測は最新の期間のエラーにより強く反応します。

segments.src: **Q3.** Your forecast has a MAPE of 5% but a large positive bias that keeps growing.
segments.tr: **Q3。**あなたの予測のMAPEは5%ですが、大きなプラスのバイアスが増え続けています。

segments.src: The most reasonable read is:
segments.tr: 最も合理的な解釈は：

segments.src: - (a) The forecast is fine — 5% is excellent
segments.tr: - (a) 予測は問題ありません。5%は優秀です

segments.src: - (b) The method is randomly noisy and needs a smaller alpha
segments.tr: - (b) 方法はランダムにノイズが多く、より小さいalphaが必要です

segments.src: - (c) You are systematically forecasting too low and should investigate the cause
segments.tr: - (c) あなたは体系的に低い予測をしており、原因を調査する必要があります

segments.src: - (d) You should switch from MAPE to MAD and move on
segments.tr: - (d) MAPEからMADに切り替えて先に進む必要があります

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日の用語

segments.src: - **Time series** — demand recorded at regular, evenly spaced intervals (weekly, monthly), the raw input to any statistical forecast.
segments.tr: - **時系列** — 定期的で均等に間隔を空けた間隔（週ごと、月ごと）で記録された需要。統計的予測への生入力。

segments.src: - **Moving average** — a forecast equal to the simple average of the last N periods; all N count equally, everything older counts not at all.
segments.tr: - **移動平均** — 最後のN期間の単純平均に等しい予測。すべてのNが等しくカウントされ、より古いものはまったくカウントされません。

segments.src: - **Exponential smoothing** — a forecast updated as `old forecast + alpha x (actual - old forecast)`, giving recent periods geometrically more weight.
segments.tr: - **指数平滑法** — `古い予測 + alpha x （実際値 - 古い予測）`として更新された予測。最近の期間に幾何級数的にさらに多くの重みを与えます。

segments.src: - **Smoothing constant (alpha)** — the 0-to-1 dial controlling responsiveness; low means stable and slow, high means reactive and jumpy.
segments.tr: - **平滑化定数（alpha）** — 反応性を制御する0から1のダイアル。低いと安定で遅く、高いと反応的で跳ねやすくなります。

segments.src: - **MAPE** — mean absolute percentage error; average miss expressed as a percent of actual demand, which makes it comparable across items but unreliable when demand is near zero.
segments.tr: - **MAPE** — 平均絶対パーセント誤差。実際の需要のパーセンテージで表現された平均的な外れ。アイテム間で比較可能にしますが、需要がゼロに近い場合は信頼性が低くなります。

segments.src: - **Bias (tracking signal)** — the running sum of signed errors, divided by MAD; it reveals whether misses are one-sided rather than merely large.
segments.tr: - **バイアス（トラッキング信号）** — 符号付き誤差の累積合計。MADで割ったもの。誤差が単に大きいのではなく、片方向であるかどうかを明らかにします。

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — (b).** A longer window averages over more history, so it smooths noise but lags real changes; more data does not guarantee lower error.
segments.tr: *回答：**Q1 — (b)。**より長いウィンドウはより多くの履歴にわたって平均化されるため、ノイズを平滑化しますが、実際の変化に遅れます。より多くのデータが必ずしも低いエラーを保証しません。

segments.src: **Q2 — O.** Alpha is the fraction of the latest error fed back into the forecast, so a bigger alpha means a bigger correction.
segments.tr: **Q2 — O。**アルファは最新のエラーの予測にフィードバックされた分数なので、大きなアルファはより大きな補正を意味します。

segments.src: **Q3 — (c).** MAD and MAPE discard the sign of the error, so a small MAPE can hide a persistent one-directional miss.
segments.tr: **Q3 — (c)。**MADとMAPEはエラーの符号を破棄するため、小さなMAPEは持続的な片方向の誤差を隠すことができます。

segments.src: A growing positive bias means actual demand keeps exceeding your forecast — a structural cause to investigate, not random noise.*
segments.tr: 増加するプラスのバイアスは、実際の需要があなたの予測を常に超えていることを意味します。ランダムなノイズではなく、調査すべき構造的な原因です。*

vi.title: [Logistics 101 #3] Mọi Dự báo Đều Sai — Đây là Cách các Chuyên gia Làm cho Chúng Ít Sai Hơn

segments.src: > Demand forecasting isn't fortune-telling; it's a set of simple arithmetic rules for turning past sales into next week's order quantity — and for measuring how badly you missed.
segments.tr: > Dự báo nhu cầu không phải là đoán định mệnh; đó là một tập hợp các quy tắc số học đơn giản để chuyển đổi doanh số quá khứ thành số lượng đặt hàng của tuần tới — và để đo lường mức độ sai lệch của bạn.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Khái niệm hôm nay

segments.src: Every business that holds inventory has to answer one question over and over: **how many should we order?** Order too many and you've buried cash in a warehouse.
segments.tr: Mỗi doanh nghiệp lưu giữ hàng tồn kho phải trả lời một câu hỏi một cách lặp đi lặp lại: **chúng ta nên đặt bao nhiêu?** Đặt quá nhiều và bạn đã chôn tiền trong kho.

segments.src: Order too few and you're apologizing to customers.
segments.tr: Đặt quá ít và bạn sẽ phải xin lỗi khách hàng.

segments.src: Nobody knows the true answer.
segments.tr: Không ai biết câu trả lời đúng.

segments.src: So supply chain planners do the next best thing: they build a **forecast** from the demand history they already have, then track how wrong it turns out to be.
segments.tr: Vì vậy, các nhà lập kế hoạch chuỗi cung ứng làm điều tiếp theo tốt nhất: họ xây dựng một **dự báo** từ lịch sử nhu cầu họ đã có, sau đó theo dõi mức độ sai lệch của nó.

segments.src: **Time series analysis** is the starting point.
segments.tr: **Phân tích chuỗi thời gian** là điểm khởi đầu.

segments.src: A time series is just demand recorded at regular intervals — units per week, cases per month.
segments.tr: Chuỗi thời gian chỉ là nhu cầu được ghi lại ở các khoảng thời gian đều đặn — đơn vị mỗi tuần, trường hợp mỗi tháng.

segments.src: Planners assume any series is a blend of four ingredients:
segments.tr: Các nhà lập kế hoạch giả định bất kỳ chuỗi nào là sự kết hợp của bốn thành phần:

segments.src: - **Level** — the baseline, "we sell about 100 a week"
segments.tr: - **Mức** — đường cơ sở, "chúng tôi bán khoảng 100 mỗi tuần"

segments.src: - **Trend** — a steady drift up or down
segments.tr: - **Xu hướng** — một sự trôi dạt ổn định lên hoặc xuống

segments.src: - **Seasonality** — a repeating pattern (December spikes, summer slumps)
segments.tr: - **Tính thời vụ** — một mô hình lặp lại (các đỉnh tháng 12, những suy giảm hè)

segments.src: - **Noise** — random wobble that will never be predictable
segments.tr: - **Nhiễu** — dao động ngẫu nhiên sẽ không bao giờ có thể dự đoán được

segments.src: The whole game is separating the signal (level, trend, seasonality) from the noise.
segments.tr: Toàn bộ trò chơi là tách biệt tín hiệu (mức, xu hướng, tính thời vụ) khỏi nhiễu.

segments.src: Forecasting methods differ mainly in *how much weight they give to recent data*.
segments.tr: Các phương pháp dự báo khác nhau chủ yếu về *mức độ trọng số mà họ dành cho dữ liệu gần đây*.

segments.src: **Moving average** is the bluntest tool.
segments.tr: **Trung bình động** là công cụ ngu ngốc nhất.

segments.src: Take the last N periods, average them, call that your forecast:
segments.tr: Lấy N kỳ cuối cùng, lấy trung bình của chúng, gọi đó là dự báo của bạn:

segments.src: Forecast for next period = (sum of last N periods) / N
segments.tr: Forecast for next period = (sum of last N periods) / N

segments.src: The only real decision is N.
segments.tr: Quyết định thực sự duy nhất là N.

segments.src: A 3-week moving average reacts fast to change but jumps around; a 12-week average is smooth and calm but slow to notice that demand has actually shifted.
segments.tr: Trung bình động 3 tuần phản ứng nhanh với thay đổi nhưng nhảy xung quanh; trung bình 12 tuần mịn và yên tĩnh nhưng chậm để nhận thấy rằng nhu cầu thực sự đã thay đổi.

segments.src: Its structural weakness: every period in the window counts equally, and everything older counts zero.
segments.tr: Điểm yếu cấu trúc của nó: mỗi kỳ trong cửa sổ tính bằng nhau, và mọi thứ cũ hơn tính bằng không.

segments.src: Last week and ten weeks ago get identical votes.
segments.tr: Tuần trước và mười tuần trước nhận được các phiếu bầu giống hệt nhau.

segments.src: **Exponential smoothing** fixes that.
segments.tr: **Làm mịn theo cấp số nhân** sửa chữa điều đó.

segments.src: It keeps one number — the previous forecast — and nudges it by a fraction of the most recent miss:
segments.tr: Nó giữ một số — dự báo trước đây — và thúc đẩy nó theo một phần của sai lệch gần đây nhất:

segments.src: New forecast = Old forecast + alpha x (Actual - Old forecast)
segments.tr: New forecast = Old forecast + alpha x (Actual - Old forecast)

segments.src: `alpha` is the **smoothing constant**, a number between 0 and 1.
segments.tr: `alpha` là **hằng số làm mịn**, một số từ 0 đến 1.

segments.src: At alpha = 0.1 the forecast barely budges; at alpha = 0.5 it chases recent sales hard.
segments.tr: Ở alpha = 0,1 dự báo hầu như không thay đổi; ở alpha = 0,5 nó theo đuổi doanh số gần đây một cách mạnh mẽ.

segments.src: Under the hood this gives every past period a weight that shrinks geometrically as it ages — recent data matters most, old data fades but never fully disappears.
segments.tr: Dưới vỏ bọc, điều này cấp cho mỗi kỳ trước đó một trọng số giảm theo hình học khi nó già đi — dữ liệu gần đây quan trọng nhất, dữ liệu cũ phai nhưng không bao giờ biến mất hoàn toàn.

segments.src: And it's cheap: you store two numbers per item, not twelve months of history.
segments.tr: Và nó rẻ: bạn lưu trữ hai số cho mỗi mục, không phải lịch sử mười hai tháng.

segments.src: That's why it runs inside most ERP systems on millions of SKUs overnight.
segments.tr: Đó là lý do tại sao nó chạy bên trong hầu hết các hệ thống ERP trên hàng triệu SKU qua đêm.

segments.src: One honest limitation: this basic version tracks level only.
segments.tr: Một hạn chế trung thực: phiên bản cơ bản này chỉ theo dõi mức độ.

segments.src: If your demand has a real trend or seasonality, plain exponential smoothing will lag behind it forever.
segments.tr: Nếu nhu cầu của bạn có xu hướng thực hoặc tính thời vụ, làm mịn theo cấp số nhân đơn giản sẽ luôn đi sau nó.

segments.src: Extended versions (Holt's method for trend, Holt-Winters for trend plus seasonality) exist precisely for that.
segments.tr: Các phiên bản mở rộng (phương pháp Holt cho xu hướng, Holt-Winters cho xu hướng cộng với tính thời vụ) tồn tại chính xác cho mục đích đó.

segments.src: Finally, **forecast error** — the part beginners skip and professionals live in.
segments.tr: Cuối cùng, **lỗi dự báo** — phần mà người mới bỏ qua và các chuyên gia sống trong.

segments.src: Two questions matter, and they're different:
segments.tr: Hai câu hỏi quan trọng, và chúng khác nhau:

segments.src: - *How far off are we?* → **MAD** (mean absolute deviation, average miss in units) or **MAPE** (mean absolute percentage error, average miss in percent)
segments.tr: - *Chúng ta sai bao xa?* → **MAD** (độ lệch tuyệt đối trung bình, trung bình sai lệch theo đơn vị) hoặc **MAPE** (lỗi phần trăm tuyệt đối trung bình, trung bình sai lệch theo phần trăm)

segments.src: - *Which direction are we off?* → **bias**, the running sum of signed errors
segments.tr: - *Chúng ta sai theo hướng nào?* → **độ lệch**, tổng chạy của các lỗi có dấu

segments.src: MAD and MAPE ignore the sign, so a +10 and a -10 look like equally good performance.
segments.tr: MAD và MAPE bỏ qua dấu hiệu, vì vậy +10 và -10 trông giống như hiệu suất tốt như nhau.

segments.src: Bias catches the thing that actually hurts: forecasting low every single week means quietly running out of stock every single week.
segments.tr: Độ lệch bắt được điều thực sự làm tổn thương: dự báo thấp mỗi tuần có nghĩa là im lặng hết hàng mỗi tuần.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Trong Đời sống Hàng ngày

segments.src: You handle replenishment for a regional coffee chain's distribution center outside Denver.
segments.tr: Bạn xử lý bổ sung cho trung tâm phân phối của một chuỗi cà phê khu vực bên ngoài Denver.

segments.src: One SKU: cases of oat milk.
segments.tr: Một SKU: các trường hợp sữa yến mạch.

segments.src: The last six weeks of actual demand: **100, 108, 96, 104, 112, 108** cases.
segments.tr: Sáu tuần gần đây của nhu cầu thực tế: **100, 108, 96, 104, 112, 108** trường hợp.

segments.src: **Moving average.** A 3-week average gives you `(104 + 112 + 108) / 3 = 108` cases for next week.
segments.tr: **Trung bình động.** Trung bình 3 tuần cho bạn `(104 + 112 + 108) / 3 = 108` trường hợp cho tuần tới.

segments.src: A 6-week average gives `104.7`.
segments.tr: Trung bình 6 tuần cho `104.7`.

segments.src: Same data, different answer — the shorter window has noticed the recent uptick, the longer one hasn't yet.
segments.tr: Dữ liệu tương tự, câu trả lời khác — cửa sổ ngắn hơn đã nhận thấy sự tăng gần đây, cửa sổ dài hơn chưa.

segments.src: **Exponential smoothing.** Your system forecast 102 for last week, actual came in at 108, so the error was +6.
segments.tr: **Làm mịn theo cấp số nhân.** Hệ thống của bạn dự báo 102 cho tuần trước, thực tế có 108, vì vậy lỗi là +6.

segments.src: With alpha = 0.2:
segments.tr: Với alpha = 0,2:

segments.src: Notice it moved only 1.2 cases, not 6.
segments.tr: Lưu ý nó chỉ di chuyển 1,2 trường hợp, không phải 6.

segments.src: That's deliberate — with alpha low, the system assumes most of that miss was noise, not a real shift.
segments.tr: Đó là cố ý — với alpha thấp, hệ thống giả định rằng hầu hết sai lệch đó là nhiễu, không phải sự thay đổi thực.

segments.src: If oat milk demand really is climbing, a 0.2 alpha will take several weeks to catch up.
segments.tr: Nếu nhu cầu sữa yến mạch thực sự đang tăng, alpha 0,2 sẽ mất vài tuần để bắt kịp.

segments.src: **Now the error check.** Over four recent weeks your errors (actual minus forecast) were **+4, -5, +12, +6**.
segments.tr: **Bây giờ kiểm tra lỗi.** Trong bốn tuần gần đây, các lỗi của bạn (thực tế trừ dự báo) là **+4, -5, +12, +6**.

segments.src: - MAD = (4 + 5 + 12 + 6) / 4 = **6.75 cases** — you're typically off by about 7 cases
segments.tr: - MAD = (4 + 5 + 12 + 6) / 4 = **6,75 trường hợp** — bạn thường sai khoảng 7 trường hợp

segments.src: - MAPE ≈ **6.3%** — respectable for a single SKU at store level
segments.tr: - MAPE ≈ **6,3%** — đáng kính trọng cho một SKU duy nhất ở mức cửa hàng

segments.src: - Bias = 4 - 5 + 12 + 6 = **+17 cases** — and *that's* the alarm
segments.tr: - Độ lệch = 4 - 5 + 12 + 6 = **+17 trường hợp** — và *đó là* cảnh báo

segments.src: Three of four weeks you forecast too low, and the misses stack up.
segments.tr: Ba trong bốn tuần bạn dự báo quá thấp, và các sai lệch cộng lại.

segments.src: A common check is the **tracking signal** (`bias divided by MAD`, here 17 / 6.75 ≈ 2.5); many planners investigate once it drifts past roughly ±4.
segments.tr: Một kiểm tra phổ biến là **tín hiệu theo dõi** (`độ lệch chia cho MAD`, ở đây 17 / 6,75 ≈ 2,5); nhiều nhà lập kế hoạch điều tra khi nó trôi dạt quá khoảng ±4.

segments.src: You're not there yet, but the direction is one-sided.
segments.tr: Bạn chưa ở đó, nhưng hướng là một chiều.

segments.src: Something real is happening — a new store on the route, a seasonal shift, a competitor closing — and no amount of tuning alpha will fix a cause your history doesn't contain yet.
segments.tr: Điều gì đó thực sự đang xảy ra — một cửa hàng mới trên tuyến, sự thay đổi thời vụ, một đối thủ cạnh tranh đóng cửa — và không có lượng điều chỉnh alpha nào sẽ sửa chữa một nguyên nhân mà lịch sử của bạn chưa chứa.

segments.src: That last move is what separates a demand planner from a spreadsheet.
segments.tr: Bước cuối cùng đó là điều tách biệt một nhà lập kế hoạch nhu cầu khỏi một bảng tính.

segments.src: The math tells you *that* you're wrong; you go find out *why*.
segments.tr: Toán học nói với bạn *rằng* bạn sai; bạn đi tìm hiểu *tại sao*.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Tóm tắt 3 dòng

segments.src: 1. A demand time series is level + trend + seasonality + noise, and forecasting means extracting the first three while ignoring the last.
segments.tr: 1. Chuỗi thời gian nhu cầu là mức + xu hướng + tính thời vụ + nhiễu, và dự báo có nghĩa là trích xuất ba cái đầu tiên trong khi bỏ qua cái cuối cùng.

segments.src: 2. Moving average weights the last N periods equally; exponential smoothing weights recent data more via `New forecast = Old forecast + alpha x error`, using far less stored data.
segments.tr: 2. Trung bình động cân nặng N kỳ cuối cùng bằng nhau; làm mịn theo cấp số nhân cân nặng dữ liệu gần đây hơn thông qua `Dự báo mới = Dự báo cũ + alpha x lỗi`, sử dụng dữ liệu lưu trữ ít hơn nhiều.

segments.src: 3. Track both size of error (MAD, MAPE) and direction of error (bias) — consistent one-sided misses mean your method is broken, not just noisy.
segments.tr: 3. Theo dõi cả kích thước lỗi (MAD, MAPE) và hướng lỗi (độ lệch) — các sai lệch một chiều nhất quán có nghĩa là phương pháp của bạn bị hỏng, không chỉ nhiễu.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Kiểm tra Tự do

segments.src: **Q1.** You switch from a 3-week moving average to a 12-week moving average.
segments.tr: **Q1.** Bạn chuyển từ trung bình động 3 tuần sang trung bình động 12 tuần.

segments.src: What happens?
segments.tr: Điều gì sẽ xảy ra?

segments.src: - (a) The forecast reacts faster to sudden demand changes
segments.tr: - (a) Dự báo phản ứng nhanh hơn với các thay đổi nhu cầu đột ngột

segments.src: - (b) The forecast becomes smoother but slower to react
segments.tr: - (b) Dự báo trở nên mịn hơn nhưng chậm phản ứng hơn

segments.src: - (c) Forecast error is guaranteed to drop
segments.tr: - (c) Lỗi dự báo được đảm bảo sẽ giảm

segments.src: - (d) Seasonality is automatically removed
segments.tr: - (d) Tính thời vụ được loại bỏ tự động

segments.src: **Q2.** In exponential smoothing, a *higher* alpha (say 0.5 instead of 0.1) makes the forecast respond more strongly to the most recent period's error.
segments.tr: **Q2.** Trong làm mịn theo cấp số nhân, một alpha *cao hơn* (nói 0,5 thay vì 0,1) làm cho dự báo phản ứng mạnh hơn với lỗi của kỳ gần đây nhất.

segments.src: **Q3.** Your forecast has a MAPE of 5% but a large positive bias that keeps growing.
segments.tr: **Q3.** Dự báo của bạn có MAPE là 5% nhưng có độ lệch tích cực lớn liên tục tăng.

segments.src: The most reasonable read is:
segments.tr: Cách đọc hợp lý nhất là:

segments.src: - (a) The forecast is fine — 5% is excellent
segments.tr: - (a) Dự báo là ổn — 5% là xuất sắc

segments.src: - (b) The method is randomly noisy and needs a smaller alpha
segments.tr: - (b) Phương pháp này có nhiễu ngẫu nhiên và cần alpha nhỏ hơn

segments.src: - (c) You are systematically forecasting too low and should investigate the cause
segments.tr: - (c) Bạn đang có hệ thống dự báo quá thấp và nên điều tra nguyên nhân

segments.src: - (d) You should switch from MAPE to MAD and move on
segments.tr: - (d) Bạn nên chuyển từ MAPE sang MAD và tiếp tục

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Các Điều khoản hôm nay

segments.src: - **Time series** — demand recorded at regular, evenly spaced intervals (weekly, monthly), the raw input to any statistical forecast.
segments.tr: - **Chuỗi thời gian** — nhu cầu được ghi lại ở các khoảng cách đều đặn, đều đặn (hàng tuần, hàng tháng), đầu vào thô cho bất kỳ dự báo thống kê nào.

segments.src: - **Moving average** — a forecast equal to the simple average of the last N periods; all N count equally, everything older counts not at all.
segments.tr: - **Trung bình động** — dự báo bằng trung bình đơn giản của N kỳ cuối cùng; tất cả N tính bằng nhau, mọi thứ cũ hơn không tính gì cả.

segments.src: - **Exponential smoothing** — a forecast updated as `old forecast + alpha x (actual - old forecast)`, giving recent periods geometrically more weight.
segments.tr: - **Làm mịn theo cấp số nhân** — dự báo được cập nhật dưới dạng `dự báo cũ + alpha x (thực tế - dự báo cũ)`, cấp cho các kỳ gần đây trọng số hơn theo hình học.

segments.src: - **Smoothing constant (alpha)** — the 0-to-1 dial controlling responsiveness; low means stable and slow, high means reactive and jumpy.
segments.tr: - **Hằng số làm mịn (alpha)** — dial 0 đến 1 kiểm soát khả năng đáp ứng; thấp có nghĩa là ổn định và chậm, cao có nghĩa là phản ứng và nhảy.

segments.src: - **MAPE** — mean absolute percentage error; average miss expressed as a percent of actual demand, which makes it comparable across items but unreliable when demand is near zero.
segments.tr: - **MAPE** — lỗi phần trăm tuyệt đối trung bình; trung bình sai lệch được biểu thị dưới dạng phần trăm nhu cầu thực tế, điều này làm cho nó có thể so sánh được trên các mục nhưng không đáng tin cậy khi nhu cầu gần bằng không.

segments.src: - **Bias (tracking signal)** — the running sum of signed errors, divided by MAD; it reveals whether misses are one-sided rather than merely large.
segments.tr: - **Độ lệch (tín hiệu theo dõi)** — tổng chạy của các lỗi có dấu, chia cho MAD; nó tiết lộ liệu các sai lệch là một chiều hơn là chỉ lớn.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — (b).** A longer window averages over more history, so it smooths noise but lags real changes; more data does not guarantee lower error.
segments.tr: *Trả lời: **Q1 — (b).** Một cửa sổ dài hơn được trung bình trên nhiều lịch sử hơn, vì vậy nó làm mịn nhiễu nhưng chậm thay đổi thực; dữ liệu nhiều hơn không đảm bảo lỗi thấp hơn.

segments.src: **Q2 — O.** Alpha is the fraction of the latest error fed back into the forecast, so a bigger alpha means a bigger correction.

de.title: [Logistik 101 #3] Jede Prognose ist falsch — So machen es die Profis weniger falsch

segments.src: > Demand forecasting isn't fortune-telling; it's a set of simple arithmetic rules for turning past sales into next week's order quantity — and for measuring how badly you missed.
segments.tr: > Nachfrageprognose ist keine Wahrsagerei; es ist eine Reihe einfacher arithmetischer Regeln, um vergangene Verkäufe in die Bestellmenge der nächsten Woche umzuwandeln — und um zu messen, wie sehr Sie daneben gelegen haben.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Heutiges Konzept

segments.src: Every business that holds inventory has to answer one question over and over: **how many should we order?** Order too many and you've buried cash in a warehouse.
segments.tr: Jedes Unternehmen, das Lagerbestände hält, muss immer wieder eine Frage beantworten: **wie viel sollten wir bestellen?** Wenn Sie zu viel bestellen, haben Sie Bargeld in einem Lagerhaus vergraben.

segments.src: Order too few and you're apologizing to customers.
segments.tr: Wenn Sie zu wenig bestellen, entschuldigen Sie sich bei Kunden.

segments.src: Nobody knows the true answer.
segments.tr: Niemand kennt die wahre Antwort.

segments.src: So supply chain planners do the next best thing: they build a **forecast** from the demand history they already have, then track how wrong it turns out to be.
segments.tr: Also tun Supply-Chain-Planer das Nächstbeste: Sie erstellen eine **Prognose** aus der bereits vorhandenen Nachfragehistorie und verfolgen dann, wie falsch sie sich herausstellt.

segments.src: **Time series analysis** is the starting point.
segments.tr: **Zeitreihenanalyse** ist der Ausgangspunkt.

segments.src: A time series is just demand recorded at regular intervals — units per week, cases per month.
segments.tr: Eine Zeitreihe ist einfach eine Nachfrage, die in regelmäßigen Abständen aufgezeichnet wird — Einheiten pro Woche, Fälle pro Monat.

segments.src: Planners assume any series is a blend of four ingredients:
segments.tr: Planer gehen davon aus, dass jede Reihe eine Mischung aus vier Zutaten ist:

segments.src: - **Level** — the baseline, "we sell about 100 a week"
segments.tr: - **Level** — die Grundlage, "wir verkaufen etwa 100 pro Woche"

segments.src: - **Trend** — a steady drift up or down
segments.tr: - **Trend** — ein konstanter Aufwärtstrend oder Abwärtstrend

segments.src: - **Seasonality** — a repeating pattern (December spikes, summer slumps)
segments.tr: - **Saisonalität** — ein sich wiederholendes Muster (Dezember-Spitzen, Sommertiefs)

segments.src: - **Noise** — random wobble that will never be predictable
segments.tr: - **Rauschen** — zufällige Schwankungen, die niemals vorhersehbar sein werden

segments.src: The whole game is separating the signal (level, trend, seasonality) from the noise.
segments.tr: Das ganze Spiel besteht darin, das Signal (Level, Trend, Saisonalität) vom Rauschen zu trennen.

segments.src: Forecasting methods differ mainly in *how much weight they give to recent data*.
segments.tr: Prognosemethoden unterscheiden sich hauptsächlich in *welches Gewicht sie den aktuellen Daten geben*.

segments.src: **Moving average** is the bluntest tool.
segments.tr: **Gleitender Durchschnitt** ist das stumpfeste Werkzeug.

segments.src: Take the last N periods, average them, call that your forecast:
segments.tr: Nehmen Sie die letzten N Perioden, berechnen Sie den Durchschnitt, nennen Sie das Ihre Prognose:

segments.src: Forecast for next period = (sum of last N periods) / N
segments.tr: Forecast for next period = (sum of last N periods) / N

segments.src: The only real decision is N.
segments.tr: Die einzige echte Entscheidung ist N.

segments.src: A 3-week moving average reacts fast to change but jumps around; a 12-week average is smooth and calm but slow to notice that demand has actually shifted.
segments.tr: Ein gleitender 3-Wochen-Durchschnitt reagiert schnell auf Veränderungen, springt aber herum; ein 12-Wochen-Durchschnitt ist glatt und ruhig, aber langsam, um zu bemerken, dass sich die Nachfrage tatsächlich verschoben hat.

segments.src: Its structural weakness: every period in the window counts equally, and everything older counts zero.
segments.tr: Seine strukturelle Schwäche: Jede Periode im Fenster zählt gleich, und alles Ältere zählt null.

segments.src: Last week and ten weeks ago get identical votes.
segments.tr: Letzte Woche und vor zehn Wochen bekommen identische Gewichte.

segments.src: **Exponential smoothing** fixes that.
segments.tr: **Exponentielle Glättung** behebt das.

segments.src: It keeps one number — the previous forecast — and nudges it by a fraction of the most recent miss:
segments.tr: Es behält eine Zahl — die vorherige Prognose — und passt sie um einen Bruchteil des letzten Fehlers an:

segments.src: New forecast = Old forecast + alpha x (Actual - Old forecast)
segments.tr: New forecast = Old forecast + alpha x (Actual - Old forecast)

segments.src: `alpha` is the **smoothing constant**, a number between 0 and 1.
segments.tr: `alpha` ist die **Glättungskonstante**, eine Zahl zwischen 0 und 1.

segments.src: At alpha = 0.1 the forecast barely budges; at alpha = 0.5 it chases recent sales hard.
segments.tr: Bei alpha = 0,1 bewegt sich die Prognose kaum; bei alpha = 0,5 verfolgt sie den neuesten Umsatz intensiv.

segments.src: Under the hood this gives every past period a weight that shrinks geometrically as it ages — recent data matters most, old data fades but never fully disappears.
segments.tr: Im Hintergrund gibt dies jedem vergangenen Zeitraum ein Gewicht, das geometrisch schrumpft, wenn es älter wird — aktuelle Daten sind am wichtigsten, alte Daten verblassen, aber verschwinden nie vollständig.

segments.src: And it's cheap: you store two numbers per item, not twelve months of history.
segments.tr: Und es ist billig: Sie speichern zwei Zahlen pro Artikel, nicht die Geschichte von zwölf Monaten.

segments.src: That's why it runs inside most ERP systems on millions of SKUs overnight.
segments.tr: Deshalb läuft es nachts in den meisten ERP-Systemen für Millionen von SKUs.

segments.src: One honest limitation: this basic version tracks level only.
segments.tr: Eine ehrliche Einschränkung: Diese grundlegende Version verfolgt nur das Level.

segments.src: If your demand has a real trend or seasonality, plain exponential smoothing will lag behind it forever.
segments.tr: Wenn Ihre Nachfrage einen echten Trend oder eine Saisonalität aufweist, wird die einfache exponentielle Glättung auf Dauer hinter ihr zurückbleiben.

segments.src: Extended versions (Holt's method for trend, Holt-Winters for trend plus seasonality) exist precisely for that.
segments.tr: Erweiterte Versionen (Holts Methode für Trend, Holt-Winters für Trend plus Saisonalität) existieren genau dafür.

segments.src: Finally, **forecast error** — the part beginners skip and professionals live in.
segments.tr: Schließlich, **Prognosefehler** — der Teil, den Anfänger überspringen und Profis darin leben.

segments.src: Two questions matter, and they're different:
segments.tr: Zwei Fragen sind wichtig, und sie sind unterschiedlich:

segments.src: - *How far off are we?* → **MAD** (mean absolute deviation, average miss in units) or **MAPE** (mean absolute percentage error, average miss in percent)
segments.tr: - *Wie weit sind wir daneben?* → **MAD** (mittlere absolute Abweichung, durchschnittlicher Fehler in Einheiten) oder **MAPE** (mittlerer absoluter prozentualer Fehler, durchschnittlicher Fehler in Prozent)

segments.src: - *Which direction are we off?* → **bias**, the running sum of signed errors
segments.tr: - *In welche Richtung sind wir daneben?* → **bias**, die laufende Summe der vorzeichenbehafteten Fehler

segments.src: MAD and MAPE ignore the sign, so a +10 and a -10 look like equally good performance.
segments.tr: MAD und MAPE ignorieren das Vorzeichen, daher sieht eine +10 und eine -10 gleich gut aus.

segments.src: Bias catches the thing that actually hurts: forecasting low every single week means quietly running out of stock every single week.
segments.tr: Bias erfasst das, was wirklich weh tut: Jede einzelne Woche zu niedrig zu prognostizieren bedeutet, jede einzelne Woche stillschweigend ohne Lagerbestand zu sein.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: You handle replenishment for a regional coffee chain's distribution center outside Denver.
segments.tr: Sie kümmern sich um die Nachschubversorgung des Distributionszentrums einer regionalen Kaffeekette außerhalb von Denver.

segments.src: One SKU: cases of oat milk.
segments.tr: Ein SKU: Fälle von Hafermilch.

segments.src: The last six weeks of actual demand: **100, 108, 96, 104, 112, 108** cases.
segments.tr: Die letzten sechs Wochen der tatsächlichen Nachfrage: **100, 108, 96, 104, 112, 108** Fälle.

segments.src: **Moving average.** A 3-week average gives you `(104 + 112 + 108) / 3 = 108` cases for next week.
segments.tr: **Gleitender Durchschnitt.** Ein 3-Wochen-Durchschnitt ergibt `(104 + 112 + 108) / 3 = 108` Fälle für die nächste Woche.

segments.src: A 6-week average gives `104.7`.
segments.tr: Ein 6-Wochen-Durchschnitt ergibt `104,7`.

segments.src: Same data, different answer — the shorter window has noticed the recent uptick, the longer one hasn't yet.
segments.tr: Gleiche Daten, andere Antwort — das kürzere Fenster hat den neuesten Anstieg bemerkt, das längere noch nicht.

segments.src: **Exponential smoothing.** Your system forecast 102 for last week, actual came in at 108, so the error was +6.
segments.tr: **Exponentielle Glättung.** Ihr System prognostizierte 102 für letzte Woche, der tatsächliche Wert lag bei 108, daher betrug der Fehler +6.

segments.src: With alpha = 0.2:
segments.tr: Mit alpha = 0,2:

segments.src: Notice it moved only 1.2 cases, not 6.
segments.tr: Beachten Sie, dass es sich nur um 1,2 Fälle bewegt hat, nicht 6.

segments.src: That's deliberate — with alpha low, the system assumes most of that miss was noise, not a real shift.
segments.tr: Das ist absichtlich — bei niedrigem alpha geht das System davon aus, dass das meiste dieses Fehlers Rauschen war, nicht eine echte Verschiebung.

segments.src: If oat milk demand really is climbing, a 0.2 alpha will take several weeks to catch up.
segments.tr: Wenn die Hafermilch-Nachfrage wirklich steigt, wird ein 0,2-Alpha mehrere Wochen brauchen, um aufzuholen.

segments.src: **Now the error check.** Over four recent weeks your errors (actual minus forecast) were **+4, -5, +12, +6**.
segments.tr: **Jetzt die Fehlerprüfung.** In den letzten vier Wochen betrugen Ihre Fehler (tatsächlich minus Prognose) **+4, -5, +12, +6**.

segments.src: - MAD = (4 + 5 + 12 + 6) / 4 = **6.75 cases** — you're typically off by about 7 cases
segments.tr: - MAD = (4 + 5 + 12 + 6) / 4 = **6,75 Fälle** — Sie sind normalerweise um etwa 7 Fälle daneben

segments.src: - MAPE ≈ **6.3%** — respectable for a single SKU at store level
segments.tr: - MAPE ≈ **6,3%** — respektabel für ein einzelnes SKU auf Geschäftsebene

segments.src: - Bias = 4 - 5 + 12 + 6 = **+17 cases** — and *that's* the alarm
segments.tr: - Bias = 4 - 5 + 12 + 6 = **+17 Fälle** — und *das* ist der Alarm

segments.src: Three of four weeks you forecast too low, and the misses stack up.
segments.tr: Drei von vier Wochen prognostizieren Sie zu niedrig, und die Fehler häufen sich.

segments.src: A common check is the **tracking signal** (`bias divided by MAD`, here 17 / 6.75 ≈ 2.5); many planners investigate once it drifts past roughly ±4.
segments.tr: Eine häufige Prüfung ist das **Verfolgungssignal** (`bias geteilt durch MAD`, hier 17 / 6,75 ≈ 2,5); viele Planer untersuchen, sobald es ungefähr ±4 überschreitet.

segments.src: You're not there yet, but the direction is one-sided.
segments.tr: Sie sind noch nicht dort, aber die Richtung ist einseitig.

segments.src: Something real is happening — a new store on the route, a seasonal shift, a competitor closing — and no amount of tuning alpha will fix a cause your history doesn't contain yet.
segments.tr: Etwas Echtes passiert — ein neuer Laden auf der Route, eine saisonale Verschiebung, ein Konkurrent schließt — und keine Menge an Alpha-Abstimmung wird eine Ursache beheben, die Ihre Geschichte noch nicht enthält.

segments.src: That last move is what separates a demand planner from a spreadsheet.
segments.tr: Dieser letzte Schritt ist das, was einen Nachfrageplaner von einer Tabelle trennt.

segments.src: The math tells you *that* you're wrong; you go find out *why*.
segments.tr: Die Mathematik sagt dir, *dass* du unrecht hast; du gehst und findest heraus *warum*.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3-Zeilen-Zusammenfassung

segments.src: 1. A demand time series is level + trend + seasonality + noise, and forecasting means extracting the first three while ignoring the last.
segments.tr: 1. Eine Nachfrage-Zeitreihe ist Level + Trend + Saisonalität + Rauschen, und Prognosen bedeuten, die ersten drei zu extrahieren, während die letzte ignoriert wird.

segments.src: 2. Moving average weights the last N periods equally; exponential smoothing weights recent data more via `New forecast = Old forecast + alpha x error`, using far less stored data.
segments.tr: 2. Der gleitende Durchschnitt wiegt die letzten N Perioden gleich; die exponentielle Glättung wiegt aktuelle Daten mehr über `Neue Prognose = Alte Prognose + alpha x Fehler`, mit viel weniger gespeicherten Daten.

segments.src: 3. Track both size of error (MAD, MAPE) and direction of error (bias) — consistent one-sided misses mean your method is broken, not just noisy.
segments.tr: 3. Verfolgen Sie sowohl die Größe des Fehlers (MAD, MAPE) als auch die Richtung des Fehlers (bias) — konsistente einseitige Fehler bedeuten, dass Ihre Methode kaputt ist, nicht nur laut.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Selbsttest

segments.src: **Q1.** You switch from a 3-week moving average to a 12-week moving average.
segments.tr: **F1.** Sie wechseln von einem 3-Wochen-Gleitdurchschnitt zu einem 12-Wochen-Gleitdurchschnitt.

segments.src: What happens?
segments.tr: Was passiert?

segments.src: - (a) The forecast reacts faster to sudden demand changes
segments.tr: - (a) Die Prognose reagiert schneller auf plötzliche Nachfrageveränderungen

segments.src: - (b) The forecast becomes smoother but slower to react
segments.tr: - (b) Die Prognose wird glatter, aber langsamer zu reagieren

segments.src: - (c) Forecast error is guaranteed to drop
segments.tr: - (c) Der Prognosefehler ist garantiert gesunken

segments.src: - (d) Seasonality is automatically removed
segments.tr: - (d) Die Saisonalität wird automatisch entfernt

segments.src: **Q2.** In exponential smoothing, a *higher* alpha (say 0.5 instead of 0.1) makes the forecast respond more strongly to the most recent period's error.
segments.tr: **F2.** Bei exponentieller Glättung führt ein *höheres* Alpha (beispielsweise 0,5 statt 0,1) dazu, dass die Prognose stärker auf den Fehler des letzten Zeitraums reagiert.

segments.src: **Q3.** Your forecast has a MAPE of 5% but a large positive bias that keeps growing.
segments.tr: **F3.** Ihre Prognose hat eine MAPE von 5%, aber einen großen positiven Bias, der weiter wächst.

segments.src: The most reasonable read is:
segments.tr: Die vernünftigste Interpretation ist:

segments.src: - (a) The forecast is fine — 5% is excellent
segments.tr: - (a) Die Prognose ist in Ordnung — 5% ist ausgezeichnet

segments.src: - (b) The method is randomly noisy and needs a smaller alpha
segments.tr: - (b) Die Methode ist zufällig laut und braucht ein kleineres Alpha

segments.src: - (c) You are systematically forecasting too low and should investigate the cause
segments.tr: - (c) Sie prognostizieren systematisch zu niedrig und sollten die Ursache untersuchen

segments.src: - (d) You should switch from MAPE to MAD and move on
segments.tr: - (d) Sie sollten von MAPE zu MAD wechseln und weitermachen

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Heutige Begriffe

segments.src: - **Time series** — demand recorded at regular, evenly spaced intervals (weekly, monthly), the raw input to any statistical forecast.
segments.tr: - **Zeitreihe** — Nachfrage, die in regelmäßigen, gleich beabstandeten Abständen (wöchentlich, monatlich) aufgezeichnet wird, die Roheingabe für jede statistische Prognose.

segments.src: - **Moving average** — a forecast equal to the simple average of the last N periods; all N count equally, everything older counts not at all.
segments.tr: - **Gleitender Durchschnitt** — eine Prognose gleich dem einfachen Durchschnitt der letzten N Perioden; alle N zählen gleich, alles Ältere zählt überhaupt nicht.

segments.src: - **Exponential smoothing** — a forecast updated as `old forecast + alpha x (actual - old forecast)`, giving recent periods geometrically more weight.
segments.tr: - **Exponentielle Glättung** — eine Prognose, die als `alte Prognose + alpha x (tatsächlich - alte Prognose)` aktualisiert wird, was den neuesten Perioden geometrisch mehr Gewicht gibt.

segments.src: - **Smoothing constant (alpha)** — the 0-to-1 dial controlling responsiveness; low means stable and slow, high means reactive and jumpy.
segments.tr: - **Glättungskonstante (alpha)** — das 0-zu-1-Einstellrad, das die Reaktionsfähigkeit steuert; niedrig bedeutet stabil und langsam, hoch bedeutet reaktiv und springend.

segments.src: - **MAPE** — mean absolute percentage error; average miss expressed as a percent of actual demand, which makes it comparable across items but unreliable when demand is near zero.
segments.tr: - **MAPE** — mittlerer absoluter prozentualer Fehler; durchschnittlicher Fehler, ausgedrückt als Prozentsatz der tatsächlichen Nachfrage, was ihn über Artikel vergleichbar macht, aber unzuverlässig, wenn die Nachfrage nahe Null liegt.

segments.src: - **Bias (tracking signal)** — the running sum of signed errors, divided by MAD; it reveals whether misses are one-sided rather than merely large.
segments.tr: - **Bias (Verfolgungssignal)** — die laufende Summe der vorzeichenbehafteten Fehler, geteilt durch MAD; sie zeigt, ob Fehler einseitig sind, anstatt nur groß zu sein.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — (b).** A longer window averages over more history, so it smooths noise but lags real changes; more data does not guarantee lower error.
segments.tr: *Antworten: **F1 — (b).** Ein längeres Fenster mittelt über mehr Geschichte, also glättet es Rauschen, aber lags echte Änderungen; mehr Daten garantieren keinen niedrigeren Fehler.

segments.src: **Q2 — O.** Alpha is the fraction of the latest error fed back into the forecast, so a bigger alpha means a bigger correction.
segments.tr: **F2 — R.** Alpha ist der Bruchteil des letzten Fehlers, der in die Prognose zurückgeführt wird, daher bedeutet ein größeres Alpha eine größere Korrektur.

segments.src: **Q3 — (c).** MAD and MAPE discard the sign of the error, so a small MAPE can hide a persistent one-directional miss.
segments.tr: **F3 — (c).** MAD und MAPE verwerfen das Vorzeichen des Fehlers, daher kann eine kleine MAPE einen hartnäckigen einseitigen Fehler verbergen.

segments.src: A growing positive bias means actual demand keeps exceeding your forecast — a structural cause to investigate, not random noise.*
segments.tr: Ein wachsender positiver Bias bedeutet, dass die tatsächliche Nachfrage Ihre Prognose immer wieder überschreitet — eine strukturelle Ursache, die untersucht werden muss, nicht nur Zufallsrauschen.*
